fetchedPapers.title: A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions
fetchedPapers.abstract: We give an algorithm for computing an $\eps$-approximate fixed point of any $d$-dimensional nonexpansion with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm in time $\log(1/\eps)^{O(\log^2 d)}$. At its core, our method uses a boosting argument to geometrically shrink a search region. Among other consequences, our algorithm implies that simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time.

fetchedPapers.title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
fetchedPapers.abstract: An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria. This mixed discriminant can be regarded as an $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for some matrix $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of [Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky 1994], and the convex hull of the columns of $\mathcal{A}$ is a polytope, which we call the Nashtope. We study this $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for each balanced game format with at least three players. This discriminant is a subset of the Nash discriminant variety introduced in [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026]. We compute the codimension and degree of this discriminant for all balanced game formats, including on-boundary formats, using the Euler obstruction formula in [Matsui--Takeuchi 2011]. Our $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant locus corresponds to a special multigraded Hurwitz locus studied in [Pratt--Sodomaco--Sturmfels 2026]. As a consequence of [Pokidkin 2026], we obtain the codimensions and degrees of the irreducible components of the Nash discriminant variety for each balanced game format with at least three players, fully resolving Problem 3.8 of [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026].

fetchedPapers.title: Computing the Nucleon of Matching Games
fetchedPapers.abstract: The nucleon is the multiplicative counterpart of the nucleolus: it lexicographically maximizes the fraction of its stand-alone value that each coalition receives. We study exact nucleon computation in matching games and in two extensions: $b$-matching games, in which players may have several partners, and partitioned matching games, in which one player may own several vertices. We resolve three open problems from a recent survey. For ordinary matching games with nonnegative rational weights, we give a polynomial-time combinatorial algorithm using maximum-weight matching, shortest paths, and minimum-cost flow, ; it returns both a nucleon allocation and a compact description of the full nucleon. In contrast, computing any nucleon allocation is NP-hard for unit-weight $b$-matching games with capacities at most three and for unit-weight partitioned matching games of width at most three. Finally, for the unresolved capacity-two case, we show that exact nucleon computation is polynomial-time Turing reducible to SHORTEST NON-ZERO CYCLE.

fetchedPapers.title: Formalizing Cooperation and Competition: An AI-Assisted Mathematical Addendum to a 2018 Planning Thesis
fetchedPapers.abstract: We present an AI-assisted mathematical addendum to Strategic Trip Planning: Striking a Balance Between Competition and Cooperation (Amar, 2018). We reconstruct selected relationships between strategic choice, cooperative stability, participant approval and enforcement. The thesis's Nash-to-core proposition is under-specified until outsider opportunities are stated. We verify two-person implications under fixed outsiders and explicit efficiency conditions. Under isolation, the original example has an empty TU core; its funded counterpart uses an explicit external subsidy. For a monotone resource model we characterize the exact financing gap. A finite negotiation procedure implemented in Lean is proved to terminate with participant approval, joint-cost non-worsening and local optimality against permitted approved moves. Supporting formalizations address bargaining geometry and regret-based efficiency. A resource-game counterinstance shows why monotonicity alone provides no uniform price-of-anarchy bound. Reproducible computations compare a documented heuristic reconstruction with the verified procedure on 44 source-based instances and 96 starting cases from four additional synthetic network families. Acceptance-matched heuristic and randomized pairwise-search controls contextualize the optimization results. The mathematical ingredients are established results; the contribution is a traceable reconstruction linking source statements, explicit assumptions, checked proofs, executable code and retained counterinstances. The study illustrates how AI-assisted investigation can turn engineering intuitions from legacy research into precise mathematical claims whose conditions and computational consequences can be inspected and reproduced.

fetchedPapers.title: GSP Autobidding Equilibria with Few Advertisers or Slots
fetchedPapers.abstract: In sponsored-shopping auctions, one advertiser may win several positions, and a product that is never displayed may determine the prices of several winners. Under generalized second-price (GSP) pricing without self-pricing, these interactions couple allocation and payment through a single global ranking. We prove that exact autobidding equilibria under budget and return-on-investment (ROI) constraints can be computed in polynomial time whenever either the number $n$ of advertisers or the number $K$ of display slots is fixed. Our algorithms rely on two structural reductions. With few advertisers, the payment polytopes of tied bid layers combine by a Minkowski sum, giving a fixed-dimensional representation of exponentially many rankings. With few slots, budget equilibria admit threshold recovery and an exact submodular description of attainable payments at the display boundary. For ROI, we prove that every group-consecutive equilibrium has a representative with at most $K+2$ nonunit multipliers, preserving the item and price in every displayed slot. In each case, the reduction leads to polynomially many systems of polynomial equations and inequalities in bounded dimension. The algorithms compute exact multipliers and explicit distributions over valid group-consecutive rankings, with support at most $n+1$; for ROI with few slots, this improves to $\min\{n+1,K+3\}$.

fetchedPapers.title: When Are We Near Nash? Certifying Solutions in General-Sum Games
fetchedPapers.abstract: Heuristic solvers for general-sum extensive-form games produce a stream of iterates, and practice reports the NashGap of the returned profile. We ask what a solver can know about its own iterates from the regret accumulators and the terminal-distribution accumulators its updates already maintain. In two-player games the NashGap of a weighted average strategy equals, at the maximizing player, the weighted external regret plus a signed value correction. Bounding the regret by the running counterfactual-regret accumulator gives an online certificate whose cost per checkpoint is linear in the number of terminal histories. The certificate stays sound under alternating updates and in games with three or more players. The mismatch between what alternation evaluates and what the averages record enters as one signed comparator term, maximized in a single backward pass per player whose comparator weight is nonzero. The bound is read off the regret state, with no best response against the average. Run a portfolio of training-free regret-matching solvers, output the iterate with the smallest certificate, and verify that iterate once. On the benchmark's biased Leduc family a pool of sixteen training-free solvers, seven original and nine recent variants, solves $89\%$ of the $64$ instances at threshold $10^{-5}$ this way, matching the trajectory-minimum union of the solvers. The same protocol solves $92\%$ of the $64$ pre-registered held-out instances and $89\%$ again on a third set of $64$ instances that no earlier stage used. The zero-best-response certificate certifies all $57$ in-sample solves and all $57$ fresh ones, and $58$ of the $59$ held-out ones. Its exact-comparator refinement certifies every solve in the three sets. The certificate states both and attributes its bound. Code is available at https://github.com/lbn187/CertNE.

fetchedPapers.title: Pareto Inefficiency of EFX
fetchedPapers.abstract: We consider the problem of allocating indivisible goods to agents with additive valuations, under two classic notions of fairness and efficiency: envy-freeness up to any good (EFX) and Pareto optimality. While some of the earliest work on EFX showed that Pareto optimal EFX allocations may not exist if agents can have zero value for some goods, it has remained open whether the same is true when all values are positive. We present a simple instance in which every good has positive value to every agent, but no Pareto optimal EFX allocation exists. We then generalize to a family of instances showing that Pareto optimal $α$-EFX allocations may not exist for any $α> 2/3$.

fetchedPapers.title: Cycle structure of best-response dynamics in random bimatrix games
fetchedPapers.abstract: We study the best-response dynamics in games with random payoffs. We consider two-player bimatrix games, with $n$ strategies each. We assume that payoffs come from a continuous distribution, and study the best-response dynamics of these games, after imposing some structure on their payoff matrices. In particular, we focus on symmetric games, antisymmetric games, common-interest games, zero-sum games, and games with independent payoffs. When two players take turns in playing the best response to the opponent's action, they eventually end up cycling through the same sequence of actions. The main focus of the paper is the cycle structure of large random games. In particular, we study the number of cycles, the number of cycles of a certain length, the length of the longest cycle, and related quantities. We show that the structure of the game has an important impact on the typical cycle structure. Our arguments are based on a representation of the best-response dynamics of these games as directed bipartite graphs, and on the cycle structure that arises in them.

fetchedPapers.title: Correlated Quantal Response Equilibrium: A New Equilibrium Notion for Human-AI Strategic Interactions
fetchedPapers.abstract: The modeling of the behavior of agents in strategic environments and the prediction of the resulting outcomes has long been a challenging problem; this has been the focus of game theory. The introduction of AI agents as human-aids or as sole decision-makers expands the underlying question: Can we model behavior and predict outcomes of strategic games that involve a mix of AI agents and human players? As an initial answer, we propose Correlated Quantal Response Equilibrium (CQRE) that combines and generalizes classical solution concepts such as Quantal Response Equilibrium and Correlated Equilibrium. We answer questions of existence and propose a method for computing the CQRE that is a best fit to a given joint action distribution. We demonstrate the empirical effectiveness of CQRE predictions using a diverse collection of complex general-sum games, including high-rank and large-action two-player games, challenging multiplayer games, and a large-scale extension of the Selten--Chmura setting to AI--AI and human--AI play.

fetchedPapers.title: Memory Manipulation
fetchedPapers.abstract: We study persuasion that works through memory: a manipulator alters the probabilities with which a Bayesian decision-maker recalls the signals he has received. The decision-maker corrects for the elevated or reduced probabilities of recalling different signals, and this correction disciplines what manipulation can achieve. Manipulation cannot move the average posterior. It backfires on decision-makers with few memories, whose sparse recall is evidence against the favored state, yet it is effective on those with many, who can be led to arbitrarily confident beliefs in the wrong state. It thickens the right tail of the belief distribution and, under Poisson memory, lowers its hazard rate. In a monopoly pricing application, the seller manipulates memory retrieval at high prices, and manipulation in turn raises the optimal price. In a narrative persuasion application, memory manipulation reduces information provision and creates echo chambers.

summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型考虑n个广告主和K个展示位，每个广告主拥有多件商品，通过统一乘数调整所有商品的出价。在GSP机制下，展示位按出价排序，点击价格为下一个不同广告主的出价。广告主受预算或ROI约束，并采用最大化出价的均衡策略。均衡由乘数配置和在有效排名上的概率分布构成，需满足支付可行性与激励相容。

summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 核心方法基于两种结构约简：当广告主少时，利用各出价层内支付矩阵的凸包组合（Minkowski和）压缩指数级排名；当展示位少时，预算情形通过阈值恢复与子模容量多面体刻画边界支付，ROI情形则证明存在仅含至多K+2个非单位乘数的代表性均衡。两者均转化为低维多项式方程组求解。

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 在一般和博弈中，计算纳什均衡是PPAD完全问题，因此实践中常使用启发式求解器并事后评估其纳什间隙（NashGap）。然而现有评测协议往往依赖于对每个检查点进行精确的最佳响应计算，成本高昂且选择规则不透明。本文指出，这种‘轨迹最小’评估隐含了一个未声明的选择规则和大量额外计算，导致报告结果难以复现和比较。因此，问题在于：能否仅利用求解器自身维护的状态，在不进行最佳响应的情况下，实时提供一个可靠且紧致的纳什间隙上界？

rawOutput.titleZh: 相关量化响应均衡：人类与人工智能战略交互的新均衡概念

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 传统博弈论中的纳什均衡难以准确预测人类在战略互动中的实际行为，而量化响应均衡（QRE）虽能刻画人类的有限理性，却忽略了玩家间的协调与行为依赖。随着大语言模型作为决策者参与战略游戏，如何统一建模人类与AI的混合交互成为新挑战。本文旨在填补一个理论空白：是否存在一种既能捕捉跨玩家行为依赖，又能允许异质性非完全服从的点预测均衡。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 作者提出了相关量化响应均衡（CQRE），将相关均衡（CE）与量化响应均衡（QRE）结合。模型允许每个玩家对每个推荐动作设置独立的‘松弛’参数，表示偏离该动作所能获得的最大期望收益。在满足这些松弛约束的联合分布集合中，CQRE选取香农熵最大的那个，即最接近均匀分布的预测。这种设定既保留了CE的协调能力，又通过松弛机制模拟了类似QRE的随机响应行为。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文证明了CQRE在任意固定松弛向量下均存在唯一解，并提出了CQRE-c（公共松弛）、CQRE-pp（逐玩家松弛）和CQRE-pa（逐玩家逐动作松弛）三种变体，形成了嵌套的模型体系。实证结果显示，CQRE-pa在拟合12个经典人类博弈数据时，KL散度比Logit-QRE降低56.9%，并在多数AI-AI和三人博弈中表现更优，显著提升了对真实联合行为分布的预测精度。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者将CQRE的求解构造成一个双层优化问题：内层对给定松弛向量求解最大熵联合分布，外层则通过最小化预测与观测分布间的KL散度来拟合最优松弛参数。内层问题被转化为带线性不等式约束的凸优化，采用序列最小二乘规划求解；外层利用隐函数微分计算梯度，结合网格搜索与L-BFGS-B算法进行多起点优化，确保稳定性与效率。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: CQRE的优势在人为构造的乘积形式人机交互数据上反而不如Logit-QRE，表明其联合分布建模特性在缺乏真实依赖时可能过拟合。此外，最大熵选择在高度集中行为下可能不够灵活。尽管如此，该模型为人类-AI混合博弈提供了首个统一的、可计算的点预测框架，其模型构建思路、双层估计方法及大规模LLM行为数据集极具阅读与借鉴价值。

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 为什么人们会因回忆方式不同而被说服？本文研究一种非传统说服机制：说服者不提供新信息，而是操纵决策者从记忆中提取信号的概率。这回应了心理学中‘可得性启发’和经济学中记忆偏差的实证发现，填补了标准贝叶斯说服模型未考虑内生记忆检索的空白。核心问题是：当个体知道自己记忆被操纵时，这种操纵还能否有效，以及它如何影响信念分布。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型设定一个贝叶斯决策者拥有由状态决定的随机信号记忆库，每个信号按与其内容相关的概率被回忆。说服者通过提高支持目标状态信号的回忆概率、降低反对信号的概率来操纵记忆提取。决策者知道操纵机制并据此理性修正信念，使用贝叶斯法则结合回忆到的信号和对未回忆可能性的认知。关键假设是回忆概率可被外部影响，且记忆规模服从类泊松分布以保证修正项有界。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文发现操纵无法改变平均后验信念，但会重塑其分布：对记忆少的人可能适得其反（稀疏回忆成为反面证据），对记忆多的人则极为有效，甚至使其在错误状态下形成高度确信。操纵使信念分布右尾变厚，在泊松记忆下还降低其风险率。这揭示了一个反直觉结论：越是见多识广者，越可能因选择性回忆陷入顽固错觉。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者通过分解后验对数几率为直接效应（已回忆信号）和间接效应（回忆难易度修正）进行分析。利用大偏差原理和鞍点逼近技术比较操纵前后极端信念的概率衰减速率。关键在于证明在大记忆量下，直接证据积累速度超过修正项的增长，从而主导信念方向。该方法系统刻画了操纵如何通过改变尾部行为影响决策。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 模型依赖类泊松记忆假设，若记忆分布尾部更重（如几何分布），修正效应可能随回忆增多而不受控，削弱结论。操纵效果也受限于信号结构，当信号完全揭示状态时增益消失。尽管如此，论文的价值在于提出了‘记忆提取操纵’这一新颖的信息设计框架，其核心模型、尾部支配结果及对专家与外行反应差异的解释极具启发性，值得细读其理论构建与均衡分析部分。

rawOutput.titleZh: 主导策略与贝叶斯机制之间的收益保证等价性

summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型考虑对称独立私有价值环境下的单物品拍卖，卖家不知道价值分布F，但知道某些顺序统计量的期望，如最高值的期望u或次高值的期望n。买家独立同分布采样自F，机制需满足激励相容和参与约束。研究比较两类机制：主导策略激励相容（DIC）与贝叶斯激励相容（BIC），关注其最坏情况下的收益表现。

fetchedPapers.title: HGM-Dual: Lineage-Aware Guided Agent Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Planning
fetchedPapers.abstract: Harness optimization, which improves an agent's prompts, tools, and workflows, is an increasingly effective way to enhance agents built on frozen or closed-source LLMs. Leading approaches such as the Darwin--Godel Machine and the Huxley--Godel Machine (HGM) rely on recursive self-improvement and were developed mainly for coding, where the competence needed to improve the agent coincides with the competence being improved. Planning tasks, in which an agent must produce a sequence of tool calls that jointly satisfies interacting constraints, break this alignment. There, open-ended self-modification repeatedly explores ineffective changes and consumes substantial evaluation budgets. We introduce HGM-Dual, a diagnostic-guided framework for budget-efficient harness evolution for planning agents. First, HGM-Dual represents agent evolution as lineage-aware context. This context records what each ancestor changed, which behaviors improved or regressed, and which modifications were ineffective, giving the editor explicit edit-outcome attribution instead of an unstructured archive of past agents. Second, HGM-Dual introduces error-conditioned dual-path child generation. For each selected parent, it generates a general child that preserves open-ended exploration and specialized children that target the harness components most likely responsible for the parent's highest-ranked constraint violations. HGM-Dual outperforms the strongest baseline by up to 14.45% relative improvement in case accuracy while matching HGM variants' final performance with 2x-4x fewer evaluation budget.

fetchedPapers.title: Bio-Inspired Auditory Processing: Coupling Parallel Resonate-and-Fire Dynamics with Ternary Recurrent Networks for Speech Recognition
fetchedPapers.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise energy-efficient inference through sparse, event-driven computation, yet remain constrained on continuous, context-dependent tasks such as automatic speech recognition (ASR). A key bottleneck is the Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron, whose membrane decay erases information across pauses and phonetic boundaries while it must both extract features and retain long-range context. Inspired by cortical separation of nonlinear filtering and somatic integration, we introduce the Spiking Ternary GRU (stGRU): a ternary-weight gated recurrent unit performs temporal filtering, while downstream Resonate-and-Fire (RF) neurons generate the binary spike stream driving the next block's event pathway. This makes binary event transmission a native training constraint rather than a separate deployment-time activation quantization step; together with ternary weights, learned projections avoid dense floating-point matrix MACs. Trained end-to-end on LibriSpeech-960, Small, Medium, and Large stGRUs reach 8.09%, 7.04%, and $6.44 \pm 0.17\%$ WER on test-clean without an external language model. To our knowledge, these are the first matrix-MAC-free spiking networks without a learned ANN sequence decoder to achieve single-digit WER on LibriSpeech. The architecture also achieves 10.88% test CER on Aishell-1 (9.28% on dev) when trained from scratch. Internally, trained networks develop a depth-graded hierarchy: shallow layers act as fast acoustic filters, while deep layers form slower semantic integrators whose latent representations segregate into part-of-speech manifolds and word-level spike events. Deep-layer firing rates follow lognormal distributions with a sparsity gradient, mirroring hierarchical processing observed in human cortex in vivo. Our biologically grounded architecture combines competitive ASR with favorable modeled compute and memory cost.

fetchedPapers.title: Probing Spatial and Spectral Grounding in EEG Foundation Models
fetchedPapers.abstract: EEG foundation models are advancing at an unprecedented pace, yet their evaluation is driven by downstream accuracy, which reveals little about whether their predictions rely on physiologically interpretable signal structure. We introduce a set of perturbation probes in two grounding axes: spatial grounding in channel identity and topographic locality, and spectral grounding in oscillatory content and waveform morphology. We apply these probes to five published EEG foundation models across motor-imagery and seizure recordings. Our experiments reveal differences in both representational sensitivity and downstream reliance. Electrode identity may be encoded without influencing downstream classification: permuting LaBraM's positional codes heavily displaced its embeddings yet reduced motor-imagery accuracy by only 1.2 points, while spectral details may be discriminable without producing specific responses to simulated clinical markers, as only REVE exceeded a spectral baseline on this task. These dissociations are hidden in common benchmarks, demonstrating how grounding probes can complement performance-based evaluation by revealing what EEG foundation models encode and what their predictions depend on.

fetchedPapers.title: BrainCodes: A Lightweight EEG Foundation Model over Discrete Neural Codes
fetchedPapers.abstract: Recent electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models increasingly emphasize model scale, potentially limiting their deployment on resource-constrained devices and in everyday environments. We argue that transferable EEG features can instead be learned with a compact architecture and introduce BrainCodes, a lightweight foundation model pretrained through self-supervised learning on more than 800 hours of recordings from over 1,000 participants. Our architecture combines a quantization-based neural tokenizer with a spatiotemporal encoder that supports arbitrary electrode configurations. The pretraining objective explicitly encourages representations that capture spatial connectivity through channel positional encoding, and sensitivity to narrowband neural oscillations through an auxiliary training objective. Our model matches or surpasses the state of the art across diverse neurophysiological monitoring tasks, including sleep staging, attention assessment, and cognitive load estimation. BrainCodes transfers effectively to low-resource wearable devices while using up to 97% fewer trainable parameters than comparable architectures. Beyond predictive accuracy, our evaluation framework characterizes the geometry and invariances of learned EEG representations across measurable spatial, temporal, and spectral signal properties.

fetchedPapers.title: Reconstruction differences rival individual differences in the fly compass connectome and break trained circuit models
fetchedPapers.abstract: Neural network models are increasingly constructed from synapse-resolution connectomes, and the same circuit is now available in reconstructions from other animals and pipelines. We do not know whether such models are dependent on the reconstruction they are built from, and whether connectome differences are biological or measurement errors. We studied the Drosophila head-direction circuit in nine versions: four flies (male CNS, hemibrain, Fly Wire, BANC) and five variants of the same fly varying only by thresholds, proofreading or synapse detection. Using wiring-based correspondences validated by anatomical labels, we place all differences on one scale. A change of synapse detection within one fly changed the circuit more than halfway to the smallest inter-fly difference on four distances; proofreading differences were smaller but depended on the metric, and left and right halves of one fly differed no more than a random half. Networks trained on each wiring to hold a cued heading developed near-perfect ring attractors, but their error increased from below 1 degree to 10-28 degrees when all weights changed by 1%. Training on each wiring did not transfer to any other connectome, including other versions of the same fly; refitting thirty cell-type gains, we repaired filtering-level differences but remaining error depended on wiring distance. Training with noise lowered precision and enhanced transfer. Imaging data indicate compasses drift smoothly and do not break; they function despite differences comparable to those of this study.Therefore, connectome-constrained models need to reflect the reconstruction they stem from and the robustness normal circuits exhibit and models lack.

fetchedPapers.title: Gate Initialisation versus Recurrent Dropout and Zoneout in Learning Long Dependencies: A Controlled Study of LSTM and GRU Networks on Synthetic Tasks
fetchedPapers.abstract: Dropout and zoneout are routinely added to long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks, but, to our knowledge, their placements have not been crossed with gate initialisation in a factorial design, and it is not known whether early gradient propagation tells which runs will learn long dependencies. We trained one-layer LSTMs and GRUs on the adding problem and on delayed recall in a factorial grid of 720 runs, crossing conventional and chrono gate initialisation with up to six recurrent regulariser placements at one rate each, with pre-specified follow-ups, and recorded how sensitive the final hidden state was to the input at every lag. Because both tasks supply fresh or exhaustive training data, the study measures the regularisers' effects on optimisation and does not assess generalisation from a finite training set. At lengths chosen to make conventional initialisation difficult, all 360 chrono-initialised runs reached the validation criterion within 5000 updates, as did 119 of 120 unregularised runs with a horizon about four times too short or too long, whereas conventionally initialised networks learned slowly or did not reach the criterion within the budget at the longer lengths. Under conventional initialisation, dropout generally delayed learning and zoneout helped only in some conditions. The early input sensitivity added little to predicting which conditions learn once the early validation loss was modelled per task, architecture and initialisation. Within conditions, a flatter early decay went with the seeds that learned, but in a pre-specified test the association was modest (concordance 0.61), condition-dependent and not robust to resampling seeds. The results support chrono initialisation, even with a rough horizon, on such tasks.

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 当前神经网络模型越来越多基于高分辨率连接组构建，但同一神经回路在不同重建版本间存在显著差异。问题是：这些差异源于生物个体变异还是重建技术误差？更重要的是，基于某一特定连接组训练的模型能否迁移到其他重建版本上？这关系到模型结论的可靠性与普适性。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 研究聚焦果蝇头部方向回路，在九种不同连接组版本上训练速率网络模型，包括四只不同果蝇的数据及同一只果蝇因突触检测、过滤或校正步骤不同产生的五种变体。模型任务是维持一个提示的方向记忆，并通过零样本迁移测试其跨连接组泛化能力。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 研究发现，仅改变突触检测方法所导致的连接组差异，已接近甚至超过不同果蝇之间的最小生物学差异。尽管各真实连接组均能训练出近乎完美的环吸引子，但模型完全无法迁移到其他连接组，即使来自同一只果蝇的不同重建版本。这表明当前训练模型极度脆弱，而真实神经系统更具鲁棒性。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者采用基于连接模式的距离度量，统一量化不同来源的差异。通过一对一神经元映射进行模型参数移植，并引入细胞类型增益重拟合与噪声训练来探索恢复性能的可能。机制验证依赖预注册的环吸引子判据，结合雅可比乘子、持续同调等动态系统分析工具。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 结论受限于现有四只果蝇与三种重建流程，跨个体比较仍混杂技术因素。未注册的探索性分析（如噪声训练）虽揭示精度-鲁棒性权衡，但缺乏理论解释。最值得读的是其严谨的问题设定、差异分解方法与对‘模型脆弱性’的深刻揭示，警示连接组模型需正视重建不确定性。

paper.title: Probing Spatial and Spectral Grounding in EEG Foundation Models

rawOutput.titleZh: 探究EEG基础模型中的空间与频谱接地

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 当前EEG基础模型虽在下游任务上表现优异，但其预测是否依赖生理上可解释的信号特征仍不清楚。传统准确率指标无法揭示模型是否真正捕捉了临床相关的空间分布或波形形态，可能导致依赖伪影的捷径学习。本文质疑仅靠性能评估的局限性，强调需探明模型编码了什么信息及其决策依赖何种信号属性。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 研究在五个公开的EEG基础模型上进行，使用运动想象与癫痫发作两类数据集。通过冻结预训练编码器并仅训练线性读出头，分别测试模型对空间位置（如电极身份、拓扑顺序）和频谱结构（如相位依赖波形、振荡节律）的敏感性。评估不仅看表征变化，更关注这些变化是否影响最终分类决策。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文发现模型表征中编码的信息与其实际决策所依赖的信息常不一致。例如某些模型强烈编码电极位置但分类不受影响，另一些能检测模拟振荡却对临床样放电无特异性响应。这表明常规基准会掩盖模型是否真正‘理解’EEG信号的关键结构，必须结合扰动探针才能全面评估。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者设计了空间与频谱两个维度的扰动探针：空间上打乱电极标签或顺序，观察嵌入变化与预测稳定性；频谱上使用相位随机化的替代数据、注入窄带振荡或临床样波形，检验模型能否超越功率谱识别细微结构。这些探针分离了‘能否访问信息’‘是否编码信息’与‘是否依赖该信息做决策’三个层次。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 结论受限于小样本临床数据与仅使用线性读出头，可能无法完全反映微调后的行为。尽管如此，该工作揭示了评测EEG模型的新维度——接地性。读者应重点关注其问题设定与探针设计，这对构建可信、可解释的神经信号AI系统具有指导意义，尤其适合关心模型真实性与临床适用性的研究者。

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 现有智能体通过修改提示、工具和流程来提升性能，但这类自改进方法在长视野规划任务中效率低下。因为规划涉及多个相互依赖的约束，盲目修改常重复无效尝试或忽略关键错误。传统方法缺乏对历史修改效果的结构化记忆，也未针对当前失败原因定向调整，导致评估资源浪费严重。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 研究基于冻结的大语言模型构建任务智能体，其行为由控制器（含提示、工具和工作流）决定。在旅行和购物两类需满足复杂全局约束的规划任务上，通过执行生成方案并用多维规则评分来评估性能。目标是在有限评估预算下找到最优控制器，衡量指标包括整体得分和完全正确率。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 提出HGM-Dual框架，在相同预算下比最强基线提升最高达14.45%的案例准确率，并以2-4倍更少预算达到相近最终性能。关键在于结合谱系感知的历史上下文与错误导向的双路径生成，显著减少冗余编辑并集中资源修复高频失效点，证明结构化进化记忆与诊断引导能大幅提升优化效率。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: HGM-Dual将进化过程建模为可解释的编辑记录，汇总祖先路径上的改动内容与成效，使编辑器避免重复失败。同时采用双路径子代生成：一条保持开放探索，另一条聚焦父代最严重的错误类别进行定向修正。两者结合平衡探索与利用，确保每次评估更具信息量。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 实验集中在特定规则驱动的规划任务，错误分类依赖预定义规则，可能限制在动态或模糊反馈场景的应用。虽有消融验证核心机制，但跨模型迁移仅测试单一替代主干。最值得阅读的是其问题抽象方式、进化上下文的设计思想及错误条件生成的实现逻辑，对构建高效自进化系统具指导意义。

summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 核心在于结合离散码预测与生理感知辅助目标：量化编码迫使模型关注判别性差异而非波形细节；通道位置编码基于电极相对位移，使模型适应任意布局；窄带扰动预测则显式增强对节律活动的敏感性。该设计规避了重建误差对频谱功率的偏倚，引导表示保留关键时空谱结构。

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 现有脑电图（EEG）基础模型往往依赖大规模参数，在资源受限设备上难以部署。传统重建式预训练目标易受高功率非周期信号主导，可能忽略对认知状态敏感的窄带振荡特征。本文旨在探索能否通过更紧凑的架构和更有针对性的训练目标，学习到既高效又生理相关的可迁移EEG表示。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型输入为多通道脑电信号，经冻结的向量量化编码器转换为离散神经码序列。主干网络采用时空分离的因子化Transformer，预测被掩码的神经码，并辅以注入窄带扰动的区域进行频率、持续时间和空间位置预测。在14项下游任务上评估线性探测与全微调性能，涵盖临床、认知与消费级硬件场景。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 提出仅含190万参数的轻量模型BrainCodes，在多数任务上达到或超越更大模型的表现，尤其在小样本与稀疏电极设置下优势显著。其表示在低资源设备上保持91%性能，并首次系统验证了EEG基础模型向消费级穿戴设备迁移的可行性，证明紧凑模型亦可具备强泛化能力。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 核心在于结合离散码预测与生理感知辅助目标：量化编码迫使模型关注判别性差异而非波形细节；通道位置编码基于电极相对位移，使模型适应任意布局；窄带扰动预测则显式增强对节律活动的敏感性。该设计规避了重建误差对频谱功率的偏倚，引导表示保留关键时空谱结构。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 尽管结果优越，但其优势在超大数据集上可能减弱，且对极短事件的捕捉能力受限于量化时间分辨率。评测虽覆盖多样任务，但临床有效性未经前瞻性验证。最值得细读的是其训练目标设计逻辑与消融分析，揭示了轻量模型成功的关键机制。
